rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient at moderate temperature to elute all 10 compounds if possible and map the overall elution window without being excessively steep or slow. This should reveal whether any peaks are unretained early or still retained into the high-organic hold, guiding the next narrowing of phi window and adjustment of slope.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only available gain is reducing t_last below 10 min without losing the weakest pair. Shortening the gradient at the same phi window and temperature is the cleanest first speed test to see how much time can be cut before the 6/7 region falls under the resolution threshold.

We are very close to the optimum, with full resolution and only 0.51 min of time penalty remaining; the limiting pair is 6/7 at R=1.59, so a one-step further reduction in tG is the fastest way to test whether t_last can drop under 10 min while keeping that pair at or above 1.5. If this breaks resolution, we can back off or use temperature/window tuning afterward.

At tG 14 the only failing pair is 6/7, so keep the fast gradient and change selectivity with a one-step lower temperature, which may improve that close pair more than it hurts runtime. This is the most direct test of whether the pair is temperature-sensitive enough to recover full resolution while staying near the 10 min target.

The tG 16 method was nearly ideal and fully resolved, so now test whether a one-step higher temperature can pull t_last below 10 min while preserving the critical mid-cluster separations. Lowering temperature hurt selectivity badly, so the opposite direction is the more promising remaining lever.

Temperature shifts worsened the critical cluster, so keep the successful 16 min, 40 C conditions and slightly narrow the gradient window from the strong end. Since the last peak elutes well before the programmed gradient ends, lowering phi1 should keep all peaks in-gradient while reducing effective steepness in the occupied region and may lift the 6/7 resolution without much cost in t_last.

Use the fully resolved 16 min, 40 C method as the base and raise phi0 one step to make the effective gradient slightly stronger from the start, which should reduce t_last with a smaller selectivity disturbance than changing temperature. This directly tests whether the critical 6/7 pair can stay at or above 1.5 while bringing the last peak to 10 min or less.

Injection 7 is essentially optimal already, so the next move is a one-step further increase in phi0 to try to shave the final 0.08 min off t_last while keeping the weakest 6/7 pair above 1.5. This is the smallest targeted change from the current best method and has a real chance to reach CRF 1.000.

We have reached the maximum CRF, so the remaining injections can map robustness around the optimum; the most informative next check is whether the current best method can be made faster without losing full resolution. Since the critical 6/7 pair is only just above threshold, shortening tG one step is the direct boundary test.

The optimum at 0.15/0.95/16/40 has little margin on the 6/7 pair, but phi0 increases have improved speed efficiently so far; one more step tests the upper boundary of that lever while staying at the fully resolving tG. This checks whether full resolution can be retained with an even shorter practical method, while likely keeping CRF at the ceiling if t_last remains under 10 min.

The best method is already at CRF 1.000, so now probe robustness in the orthogonal direction by trimming phi1 one step while keeping the successful phi0 and tG. This slightly narrows the gradient window and should strengthen spreading in the critical mid-cluster, showing whether the top end can be compressed without pushing t_last back above 10 min too much.

Continue the phi1 boundary check from the robust 0.15/0.90/16/40 run by trimming the strong end one more step. This will show whether the improved 6/7 margin can be maintained while still keeping the last peak within 10 min, and it maps how tightly the upper gradient limit can be set around the actual elution window.

The best method is established, so use remaining injections to characterize robustness; a one-step temperature increase from the optimum tests whether small thermal changes preserve full resolution or sharply disturb the critical 6/7 pair. We already know 45 C was harmful at lower phi0, so this checks whether the improved phi0=0.15 setting buffers that effect.

We now know +5 C from the optimum badly collapses the critical pair; checking -5 C completes the temperature robustness map around the best method. This determines whether the optimum is specifically centered at 40 C or whether lower temperature preserves selectivity while only modestly lengthening the run.

The optimum is known, so use remaining runs to map a locally robust design space; combining the near-best phi0 and phi1 settings tests whether a slightly narrower centered window can preserve full resolution. This also checks whether the gains from higher phi0 and lower phi1 offset each other around the critical 6/7 pair.

With the maximum CRF already achieved, the most useful remaining information is robustness of the optimum to slightly shallower slope. Extending tG one step from the best method should increase margin on the critical 6/7 pair and confirms the local tradeoff surface around the chosen operating point.

This extends the local map around the optimum by pairing a slightly lower phi0 with the longer tG, testing whether extra slope margin can recover robustness without unacceptable runtime. It helps define the resolution-time tradeoff surface around the best operating region centered near phi0 0.10–0.15 and tG 16–18.

Test the opposite corner of the local design space around the optimum by combining the higher phi0 that shortened runtime with the lower phi1 that improved the critical 6/7 pair. This will show whether those two favorable trends can be balanced to retain full resolution while keeping the method comfortably under 10 min.

Injection 18 reached the CRF ceiling with the weakest pair right at the threshold, so the next informative boundary test is one more step higher in phi0 at the same narrower window. This probes whether the method can be made even stronger/faster before the first peaks become too compressed or the 6/7 pair falls below 1.5.

Injection 18 is a second optimum and sits on the 6/7 boundary, so lengthening tG one step at the same window will test whether that method has a more robust slope margin than the original optimum. This distinguishes whether 0.20/0.90 is just a sharp optimum or a broader operating region for routine use.

Injection 18 is a ceiling-scoring method with the critical pair barely above threshold, so the remaining key boundary test is whether this window can tolerate a shorter tG. This directly compares the slope sensitivity of the second optimum against the original 0.15/0.95 optimum and shows whether either can support a faster routine method.

Use a remaining run to fill the lower-left part of the local window map, combining the lower phi0 with the tighter upper limit. This helps confirm whether the best performance truly requires a relatively strong starting composition, rather than just a narrowed overall window.

This final unexplored local corner combines the stronger start that improved runtime with the tighter upper limit that improved the critical-pair margin. It directly tests whether 0.20/0.90 can be tightened further while still retaining full resolution and a sub-10 min last peak.

With two injections left and the optimum already found, the most informative remaining untested boundary is the stronger start at the wider upper limit. This isolates whether the early-pair collapse seen at phi0 0.25 with phi1 0.90 was mainly caused by the narrow window or by phi0 itself.

For the final run, test the remaining untried fast variant closest to the robust high-scoring region: lowering phi1 from the 0.15/0.95/14 method may recover the critical 6/7 pair while keeping t_last well below 10 min. This is the best last chance to see whether any 14 min gradient can still achieve full resolution near the optimum window.
